Header: Redwood All-Hands - 2026-03-22 11:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samira (CEO), Evan (COO), Priya (VP Eng), Maya (Prod), Ravi (Research), Alex (Sales), Liam (SRE), + ~120 company members on Zoom

[00:00] Samira Gupta: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick slide deck up, um, we wanted to start with a high level — Q1 in summary, good momentum, some execution gaps but overall on track.
[00:22] Samira: Quick housekeeping — recording is on, Q&A in chat, we’ll keep the first 35 minutes for leadership updates then open floor.
[00:38] Evan Rivers: Hi team. Revenue — we finished Q1 at 12% above plan, renewals are healthy, expand motions picking up with Dedicated discussions. That said, we saw a few larger deals move slower because of procurement cycles, legal reviews, and VPC questions.
[01:05] Alex Moreno: On the GTM side we've closed three pilot commitments for Dedicated capacity and two Private pilots with regulator-facing customers in EMEA — that pipeline helped the beat.
[01:24] Audience Member 1: Congrats on the pilots. Any color on timelines for dedicated GA?
[01:31] Priya Shah: Yeah thanks. From product/eng, Dedicated GA is on a staged rollout. We did closed beta in Feb, working through autoscaling and instance placement bugs. Expecting broader availability in May for targeted customers; general availability later in June.
[01:51] Priya: We continue to prioritize latency SLOs: lower 99th p95 tail through improved kv-cache warmup and continuous batching heuristics. Some of the perf wins came from kernel selector improvements.
[02:12] Samira: Nice. Quick bump about Redwood Optimize — Maya?
[02:20] Maya Chen: Optimize launches a new recommendations UI this week; it'll surface batching, quantization, and caching suggestions per route. We showed an internal demo and saw a 15–25% estimated cost reduction on a few customer workloads. Note these are estimates, we'll back them with more benchmarks.
[02:46] Ravi Desai: For model onboarding, research is focusing on quantization tradeoffs and fidelity tests. We saw one case where 4-bit quant gave a small perf hit on retrieval accuracy — we're building eval suites to catch regressions earlier.
[03:08] Evan: On security & compliance — update?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: SOC 2 Type II audit readiness is progressing. We're finalizing log retention and audit playbooks. SSO/SAML improvements and granular RBAC deployed to staging; KMS integration work is in progress with one partner for HSM-backed key wraps.
[03:30] Audience Member 2 (chat): Will private deployments require a separate license?
[03:33] Samira: Yes there's an enterprise licensing model for Private plus a platform fee; we'll share pricing tiers post all-hands.
[03:41] Alex: Quick commercial note — if you’re an AE and have prospects asking about data residency or KMS, loop in security early. We have a partner handoff pack coming.
[03:55] Priya: Technical deep dive, sorry, quick clarifying: when we say Private pilot for EMEA customers, it's a VPC-controlled control plane, customer-managed infra, and optional on-prem components for air-gapped. We’ve done two customer installs in staging.
[04:18] Alex: Good to highlight because procurement is asking for that in RFPs.
[04:24] Samira: Hiring — Fernanda?
[04:26] Fernanda Ortiz: We’re ramping hiring for infra and platform engineering. Priority roles are backend infra (8), Site Reliability (3), and solutions engineers (3). Interview loops are being standardized; feedback cycles shortened to two weeks for MCL.
[04:44] Audience Member 3: Any changes to remote/hybrid policy?
[04:47] Fernanda: No major changes; we are continuing hybrid with focus on team retreats and async collaboration improvements.
[04:55] Samira: Customer highlights — Alex, go.
[04:59] Alex: Two customer stories: a fintech in EMEA choosing Private for regulatory audits; and a consumer app choosing Dedicated because they needed predictable throughput for peak hours. Both cited our observability/tracing as key.
[05:16] Alex: Also partner update — working with a cloud partner on optimized instance types (NV switches) that give a 10–12% perf boost on longer context lengths.
[05:31] Audience Member 4: Competitor question — how are we positioning vs Anthropic and OpenAI for compliance-sensitive customers?
[05:38] Samira: We emphasize deployment flexibility and cost controls. Anthropic/OpenAI often provide hosted endpoints; our differentiator is the unified runtime + Private options + strong cost tooling. But we watch model parity carefully.
[05:52] Priya: From an engineering viewpoint, we optimize for inference economics — batching, kv cache, quantization profiles — which help customers cost compare across providers.
[06:07] Samira: Okay moving on to ops notes — Liam?
[06:10] Liam: Brief incident retrospective: March 10th latency spike — root cause was a KV cache coldstart combined with a misrouted canary autoscaler job. We’ve pushed fixes: better prefix caching, fallbacks to smaller batch sizes, and a safety circuit-breaker. Post-fix we saw 40% reduction in 99th.
[06:34] Liam: Will share incident doc and dashboard link after this meeting.
[06:38] Audience Member 5: Any change to SLAs?
[06:41] Evan: No changes to published SLAs. For Dedicated we’ll have contractual SLOs, will work through legal.
[06:48] Samira: Ok product roadmap quick hit — Maya?
[06:51] Maya: Roadmap highlights: Q2 focus is Dedicated GA, Private packaging, and Optimize feature set. Q3 we plan a rollout of model variant routing (cost/latency policy) and enhanced traceability for eval-based regression alerts.
[07:12] Maya: Also investments in evals pipeline to detect hallucination/regression on PRs. That'll reduce manual review cycles.
[07:25] Audience Member 6: Will rollout affect pricing?
[07:28] Alex: Pricing for Dedicated will be reserved capacity contracts; we'll publish sample TCO spreadsheets for common workloads. For Private, enterprise licensing plus platform fee.
[07:39] Samira: Quick org note: we’re consolidating inference infra and runtime teams into a single infra platform org to accelerate kernel work and better own perf. Priya will lead this constellation.
[07:54] Priya: Yep, goal is fewer handoffs between runtime and infra teams. We'll post org chart this week.
[08:02] Audience Member 7: Anything on observability fidelity?
[08:05] Maya: We’re increasing retention for per-route traces in paid tiers and adding token-level cost breakdown in console. Expect a beta early Q3.
[08:18] Samira: Great. Now questions from chat, gonna take a few:
[08:22] Chat - Question: Can SEs get a deeper private demo?
[08:25] Priya: Yes, we’ll schedule internal demos; sign-up link after the meeting.
[08:29] Chat - Question: Are we open-sourcing any runtime parts?
[08:32] Ravi: We’re evaluating contributions — some tooling and benchmark harnesses are likely to be OSS, core runtime remains internal for now.
[08:40] Samira: Final bit — finances. Evan?
[08:43] Evan: Burn is roughly in line with plan; sustained ops investment for Dedicated and Private is the main driver. We expect margin expansion in H2 as Optimize and Dedicated adoption improves cost per token economics.
[09:02] Evan: We’re also tightening discretionary spend and prioritizing hires that unblock revenue.
[09:12] Samira: Closing remarks: big thanks, we hit some targets and learned from a few stumbles — keep customer empathy high, keep shipping.
[09:22] Samira: Quick recap of next steps — Priya to push deck, Maya to share roadmap, Liam to post incident doc, Fernanda to finalize hire list, Alex to send top customer highlights.
[09:40] Samira: Ok we'll open the floor for live Q&A — please keep questions focused.
[09:50] Q&A section (selected):
[09:50] Audience Member 8: Will we support model tool-calling like in hosted APIs for Private?
[09:54] Priya: Yes tool-calling and structured output support are in the Private feature set; it requires a small agent runtime to be deployed with the customer's control plane.
[10:05] Audience Member 9: Any notes on model variants and fallback?
[10:09] Maya: We’ll have policy-driven routing: route by latency, cost, or quality; automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity constrained.
[10:20] Audience Member 10: What should AEs emphasize in demos?
[10:24] Alex: Emphasize deterministic economics (TCO), deployment options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and our observability features. Also highlight that we can run benchmarks during POCs.
[10:38] Samira: Thank you all. We’ll close at the top of the hour.
[10:45] End: meeting ends, recording stops.

Notes: transcript auto-generated, occasional mis-attributions and imperfect punctuation. Links referenced: Q1 deck (link posted in #all-hands), Private pilot demo recording (internal link), Incident postmortem doc (to be posted).
